G2.name: Host CPU lacks legal ROL A ($2A)
G2.mechanism: New content code executes ROL A at $11BB. The Atari instruction is legal; scripts/nmos6502.mjs lacks its definition. Most of these tests first need the phase correction; plasma boot already enters real start_gameplay, catches the host exception and reports sector 0. Adding host ROL A resolves these tests without assertion edits.

This follows the accepted two-frame Heavy-clear admission guard, but requires fixture time modelling or a separately reviewed expectation, not missing disk sectors.

G4.mechanism: After phase and host ROL correction, the accepted 120-row pre-capital departure runway blocks new Heavy admission before the old stream completes. These are gameplay expectation effects, not disk/SIO fixture omissions.

G5.name: L2 INIT isolated as a disk-free 45-cycle call
G5.mechanism: bossGateMemory already loaded the content and set GAMEPLAY. The test clears L2_VALID and calls $1900 on a CPU with no POKEY/PIA hooks. New INIT tries another checked content read. Default memory cannot complete the protocol; call reaches four-million-step limit. Supplying the real ATR-backed Drive alone makes INIT return, but test still fails: 313589 instruction cycles versus 45. The added checked read changes what that measurement contains.
